nodes.label: Smart Life QR Sign-In
nodes.rationale: A User Code plus a QR scan with the phone app, requiring no Tuya developer account; it is the same sign-in the Home Assistant Tuya integration uses.

nodes.label: Swift Port of tuya-device-sharing-sdk
nodes.rationale: SmartLifeService.swift ports Tuya's open-source tuya-device-sharing-sdk, the library behind Home Assistant's Tuya integration, and presents the same client identifier to Tuya, so the app speaks a protocol that already works with that account type.

nodes.label: AES-GCM + HMAC-SHA256 Request Envelope
nodes.rationale: Requests are AES-GCM encrypted and HMAC-SHA256 signed, matching what Tuya's own client does.

nodes.label: 12-Second State Polling
nodes.rationale: While the panel is open the app reads every linked device's state every 12 seconds, so changes made in the phone app or on a wall switch show up; Tuya's cloud offers no local event stream.

nodes.label: Infrared AC as Tuya Virtual Remote
nodes.rationale: An IR-blaster AC has no state of its own: Tuya keeps a virtual remote in the cloud and each change is a key press, so mode and temperature changes are two transmissions a second apart, nothing is sent while off, and the panel shows only what was last sent.

nodes.label: 2008 Refusal Replay
nodes.rationale: If the cloud answers 2008 the state it remembers usually differs from the app's, so the app re-sends its whole state (power, mode, temperature, fan) and tries once more; a second refusal means that remote has no code for the setting and the panel says so and reverts.

nodes.label: Tuya Error Codes 2001 / 2008 / 1109
nodes.rationale: 2001 offline, 2008 command or value not supported, 1109 invalid parameter (usually several IR keys in one request); each maps to a specific user action.

nodes.label: Alternative Tuya Cloud Project Client
nodes.rationale: A cloud project with Access ID, Access Secret and data center can be used instead, but the QR sign-in takes precedence and TuyaService.swift has seen far less real-world use than the QR route.

nodes.label: Per-Device Command Queue and Store Coalescing
nodes.rationale: AppDelegate queues commands per device, polls state and reports results to the panel, while web/src/store.js coalesces changes into few commands and rolls back ones a device refuses, so dragging a slider does not flood the cloud.

nodes.label: Capability to Tuya Data Point Mapping
nodes.rationale: Value ranges come from each device's own specification, so bulbs with a 0–255 scale and bulbs with a 10–1000 scale behave the same, and an AC shows only the controls its device has a function for.
